decided.question: how does a case reach a second live client invitation token for an address, given that minting a second invitation supersedes the first
decided.chose: invitation time inspects no ClientMembership, so a second token is minted after the first has been accepted, and the refusal is the accept transaction's 409 accountIsClient; TC-02-INT-16 now mints, re-mints, accepts the surviving token, accepts the superseded one for 400 INVITE_MESSAGES.tokenInvalid, then mints a third for the now-active client user and accepts it for 409 accountIsClient
decided.rejected: a mirror alreadyMember refusal at invitation time for an active ClientMembership, which would need a message this spec does not define and would make edge cases 2 and 21 unreachable
decided.why: rule 1 — the invite handler's already-a-member refusal reads active Membership rows only, and this spec had taken no contrary position; requirement 2 already places the one-active-principal guarantee in the accept transaction
decided.recordedAt: requirement 19a, with the superseded-token answer added to requirement 19 and to the Decided clause of edge case 21; observed by TC-02-INT-16

decided.question: does POST /api/invitations keep its present refusal message for a caller without permission, or answer this spec's manageForbidden
decided.chose: the refusal is chosen by the role in the body — role = 'client' answers 403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.manageForbidden; any body that does not carry role = 'client' keeps 403 INVITE_MESSAGES.permissionDenied unchanged; who may invite does not change
decided.rejected: answering permissionDenied for a client invitation too, which would leave manageForbidden unreachable on this route and name the wrong permission
decided.why: rule 4 — the narrower change, scoped to the one body shape this spec introduces, leaves every existing caller's refusal exactly as it is
decided.recordedAt: the Decided paragraph under `POST /api/invitations` (extended) in API Contracts; observed by TC-02-INT-02, whose steps now cover both branches, and restated in the Reused, not added message table
